[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r1] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | A skilled imitator may be described as a learner who follows a predecessor accurately, so a craft comes to be called that predecessor’s work.

[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r4] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | Hidden similarities already have a rational basis; the critic earns praise by finding them through difficult thought, like discovering a pearl rather than creating its value.

[ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Each side, believers and disbelievers, awaits the outcome of its affair; mutarabbis is the predicate of kull and is singular to match kull’s grammatical form.
[ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r10] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | On the main parsing, both man clauses are interrogative subjects with following predicates; together they fill the suspended verb’s two objects, or its one object if ʿalima means to know.

[ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r14] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · الطيبي | reports | Al-Tibi sees the ending as answering the opening: after bearing the burden of proclamation without exhausting oneself, the Prophet should worship within his capacity and leave those whom warning will not benefit; they will regret their opposition.

[ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · الجحدري وابن يعمر | reports | Al-Jaḥdarī and Ibn Yaʿmar read al-sūʾā, a feminine form of al-aswaʾ, with feminine agreement because ṣirāṭ may be feminine.
[ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas reads al-sūʾ, meaning evil.
[ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · أبو حيان | prefers | For the variant al-suyy with doubled yāʾ, Abu Hayyan prefers deriving it as a diminutive of sawāʾ, like ʿaṭā becoming ʿaṭiyy, because a diminutive of the proposed form should retain its hamza.
[ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | The author reports the objection that exchanging the hamza for yāʾ is permissible, and another al-suyy reading with doubled wāw is explained as a softened al-sūʾā.
[ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r9] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Wa-man ihtadā means whoever was guided out of error; the comparison implicit in this wording is absent in the majority reading and in the first anomalous reading.
[ALUSI-FULL:v16p289#2/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The connection of Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ to the preceding sūra is self-evident.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p349/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The ending closes the debate and echoes the opening: the Prophet has delivered guidance, so he may take comfort in completing his mission while the heedless remain astray until truth becomes clear. | mentions 20:2, 20:3
[TABATABAI:20:134-135/r3] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Tarabbus means waiting, and the straight path is the upright road; each side waits for its desired outcome and follows a way toward it.
